prompts.oak:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Asset type: orthographic top-down stone-hatchet stump cut material source. Edit the supplied source image, preserve the position, size, perimeter, bark exterior and existing off-centre torn fibre hinge EXACTLY. Retain the crisp natural wood fibres, detailed bark texture and overall species colours. Improve only the cut surface: make SIX broad irregular wedge-shaped hatchet facets, not many narrow fan wedges, meeting along the existing torn hinge. Each has its own subtly different material tone and visible abrupt broken edge. Add many fine natural slightly irregular eccentric concentric growth rings clearly visible across the smoother facets, broken and offset where a facet edge cuts through them; rings run in circular arcs ACROSS the wedges rather than following their radial direction. Rings are delicate few-percent darker pigment, not thick outlined circles. Chip off the bark at 5 irregular edge impacts, exposing small angular notches of fresh wood in the rim, with nearby raised ragged bark flakes. Flat diffuse neutral unlit texture painting, no directional illumination, no shadows or specular highlights, no text, no labels, no scenery. Square full-size output, precise overhead orthographic view.
Dense live oak. Pale sapwood #DCC296, fibres #EAD6B1, dark bark #493F34. Replace the existing huge jagged polygon of heartwood with a rounded somewhat eccentric brown #AE855B core, about 55% of wood diameter, whose irregular boundary follows a growth ring; gently varied brown within core with rings. Include 4 fine branching radial drying checks running outward from the off-centre pith through the heartwood. Dense narrow rings most legible across the pale sapwood. Preserve the torn hinge slanting from centre toward upper right.
